candidate_papers.title: MR.Q: A Model-Free Deep RL Algorithm with Model-Based Representations

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Limited evaluation to a small set of benchmarks (Gym, DMC, Atari) which are relatively homogeneous environments, questioning the generality of the method
extracted_weaknesses.quote: The authors only conducted experiments on the Gym, DMC, and Atari benchmarks, which are classic but relatively homogeneous environments. Claiming generality might be overstated given these limited evaluation.

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Hyperparameters of baseline algorithms are not properly disclosed, making it unclear if comparisons are fair and whether baselines are properly tuned
extracted_weaknesses.quote: the paper provides no detail (that I could find) regarding the hyperparameter settings of the baseline algorithms, nor how or if they were tuned. This is a critical weakness of the paper, as the possibility of untuned baselines undermines the claimed performance improvements.

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: No evidence that MR.Q is less hyperparameter sensitive than baselines or achieves better performance under equal conditions
extracted_weaknesses.quote: Do you have evidence that A) MR.Q is less hyperparameter sensitive than baselines, or B) the best single set of hyperparameters for MR.Q achieves higher performance than the equivalent for a baseline?

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Missing comparisons with important baseline algorithms like PPO, which is the most general-purpose RL algorithm in the literature
extracted_weaknesses.quote: Some key algorithms are missing, most notably PPO. It is not expected that the authors compare to every popular RL algorithm, but PPO is undoubtedly the closest thing to a 'general-purpose' RL algorithm in current literature.

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Ablation studies lack statistical significance testing and provide limited insights into individual component contributions
extracted_weaknesses.quote: The ablation study fails to provide the statistical significance of the results and lacks analysis. Furthermore, the 'reverting to theory' ablations are highly unsurprising so provide little contribution, and many of the remaining ablations show minimal performance gains.

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Method has a large list of hyperparameters which limits practical applicability and may make results sensitive to tuning
extracted_weaknesses.quote: The proposed approach comes with a large list of hyperparameters, which may limits its practical applicability.

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Different model sizes used for different baselines without normalization, making direct performance comparison unclear
extracted_weaknesses.quote: the paper seems to maintain model sizes from the original implementations of each algorithm. However, the size of the model is not defined by the algorithm, so it would be much more convincing to normalize the parameter count between algorithms and show that MR.Q achieves superior performance at the same size, or has a better scaling curve.

candidate_papers.title: Process Advantage Verifiers (PAVs) for RL with LLMs

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Experiments are limited to a single model family (Gemma) and single task domain (mathematical reasoning), limiting generalization claims
extracted_weaknesses.quote: Evaluation only on mathematical reasoning tasks... All experiments on a single model family (Gemma)

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Limited comparison with other process reward model (PRM) approaches; mostly compared against outcome reward models (ORMs) which are not the closest baseline
extracted_weaknesses.quote: I believe that a fair comparison would be to use PRMs since they are the closest possible baseline. The authors do prempt this by stating that PRMs have only demonstrated 1-2% improvement w.r.t. ORMs but that is in the context of best-of-N search. There are no comparisons with PRMs except for Fig 5a.

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Claims of exploration benefits are not convincingly justified compared to alternative exploration techniques already studied in RL
extracted_weaknesses.quote: I had trouble understanding when (or whether) introducing the sub-optimal verifier can result in a worse behavior, or when does E[V^{t+1} - V^t] < 0. Some confusion arose because the verifier is initially assumed to be just a fixed μ, while it is actually μ(π_t)

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Unclear computational overhead of training and using PAVs compared to traditional process reward models
extracted_weaknesses.quote: Could you clarify the computational overhead of training and using PAVs compared to traditional ORMs?

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Improvements on non-MATH benchmarks are marginal and paper lacks evaluation on diverse reasoning domains
extracted_weaknesses.quote: It would be helpful if you include baseline methods such as Wang et al. (2024), Shao et al. (2024) or Luo et al. (2024) to demonstrate how they perform poorly compare to your method

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Increasing synthetic data ratio does not benefit all methods equally; trend is inconsistent and lacks clear intuition
extracted_weaknesses.quote: Increasing Synthetic Data ratio does not benefit PGR and the unconditional baseline (SynthER) equally. PGR scales better at r=0.75 than SYNTHER but neither benefits from 0.875. We would think the trend would be consistent? whats the intution behind this?

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Method relies on accurately learned dynamics model, which may be challenging in complex environments and affects robustness
extracted_weaknesses.quote: The curiosity-based relevance function relies on a learned dynamics model, which might be challenging to train accurately in complex environments.

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Unclear how method scales to complex environments where diverse samples alone may not equal usefulness (e.g., noisy TV problem)
extracted_weaknesses.quote: How do you think the method would do when simply having diverse samples does not imply usefulness? An example is the noisy tv problem.

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Potential for extension to offline RL is uncertain and modifications needed are not clearly specified
extracted_weaknesses.quote: Could PGR be extended to offline RL settings? If so, what modifications would be necessary?

candidate_papers.title: Decision Transformer for Fault Detection in UTM Systems
relevant_weakness_themes: inference cost not considered in scaling law

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Evaluation conducted entirely in simulated controlled environments with no real-world empirical study or case studies
extracted_weaknesses.quote: I am particularly interested in whether the authors could include a realistic or real-world case study to complement their evaluation. As presented, the submission's evaluation appears to be conducted solely within simulated, controlled environments, which may not fully capture the complexities or variances that arise in real-world scenarios.

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Scaling law analysis does not account for inference time costs; practical deployment constraints unclear
extracted_weaknesses.quote: The evaluation metrics introduced by the author do not seem to take into account the cost of model inference. If it is taken into account, will the observed scaling law still hold? Or will Sweetspot be a specific model size?

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Sim2Real gap and transfer from simulation to real-world applications not adequately addressed
extracted_weaknesses.quote: Additionally, I would encourage the authors to address the Sim2Real (simulation-to-reality) gap, which often poses a significant challenge when transferring solutions from simulated environments to real-world applications.

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Design choices and implementation details are vague, making reproducibility difficult
extracted_weaknesses.quote: The description of the state, action, and reward is too general, making it difficult to grasp the specific types of faults being tested and their impact on the UTM system.

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: No comparison with recent ML-based testing approaches; baseline selection not justified
extracted_weaknesses.quote: Missing comparisons with other ML-based testing approaches (e.g., RNNs, LSTMs).

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Evaluation limited to outdated architectures (AlexNet, VGG-16) that are far from state-of-the-art; no scaling to modern networks
extracted_weaknesses.quote: the authors claim that they only test on AlexNet, VGG-16, and a two layer CNN due to the better alignment of these architectures with biology; however, I find this argument extremely weak... if the authors are shooting for biological plausibility (which they mention many times), then at the very least they should work with architectures like the CorNet which attempt to better align with visual cortex.

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Performance gains not justified in terms of compute cost; no comparison with compute-matched baselines
extracted_weaknesses.quote: in Table 3, we see that per epoch, the VGG model with the CH-divnorm is approximately 50% slower than the baseline, yet the performance gain is 2%. I would like to know whether similar gains can be achieved by training a compute-matched baseline.

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Evaluation limited to narrow set of tasks (CIFAR, ImageNet) without testing on transfer learning or out-of-distribution tasks
extracted_weaknesses.quote: For example, do you see gains from CH-divnorm when evaluating linear classification performance on other transfer tasks like DTD (textures), Cars/Birds etc. (fine grained classification) and other OOD evals that are commonly used for transfer learning?

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Missing comparisons with other normalization techniques that provide similar improvements
extracted_weaknesses.quote: there are other prior works that have shown significant improvements over baseline with divisive normalization such as [1]. In Ren et al, in fact, they find that simple modifications of BatchNorm and LocalNorm give large improvements over their baseline BN/LN formulations.

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Robustness results only evaluated on limited architectures and corruption severity levels
extracted_weaknesses.quote: For ImageNet-C I don't understand why the authors only evaluate their AlexNet model. Do these results also hold with VGG-16?

candidate_papers.title: Off-Policy Learning for Large Action Spaces (POTEC)

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Method assumes specific hierarchical structure in rewards and logging policy; unclear how it generalizes to different reward structures
extracted_weaknesses.quote: What if the reward is not in this hierarchy way? For example, if the reward function is just defined as r(x,a) instead of the reward of cluster + reward of the action. Or, in other words, what if the logging policy is not defined as Eq.(11)?

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: No guidance on how to select number of clusters in real-world applications; crucial hyperparameter choice
extracted_weaknesses.quote: How do you choose the number of cluster C? ... The authors could provide more details on how to select the number of clusters in the real-world applications.

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Impact of different clustering algorithms on performance not systematically studied
extracted_weaknesses.quote: The paper did not specify how different clustering algorithm could impact the performance of POTEC from both theoretical point of view and empirical study.

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Limited exploration of different logging policies and their effects on the algorithm
extracted_weaknesses.quote: They did not experiment with other logging policy settings.

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Paper claims to improve convergence rates but comparisons with existing literature are unclear and not well-positioned
extracted_weaknesses.quote: The main theoretical implications of this paper need to be explained more clearly. The authors mention they proved theoretical guarantees of *improved* convergence rate. It is unclear what works/results this paper is comparing with.

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Sequential unconfoundedness assumption may be restrictive for RL settings and requires better justification
extracted_weaknesses.quote: Assumption 1 (sequential unconfoundedness) needs justification. While it may be natural for other settings, whether this assumption is proper in RL is unclear. The assumption suggests actions only affect rewards but not the Markovian dynamic, which seems restrictive.

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Experiments only evaluate Q-difference estimation accuracy, not actual policy learning performance
extracted_weaknesses.quote: My understanding is that the ultimate goal of the authors' approach is to obtain better RL policies, i.e., estimating difference of Q is only a means towards this ultimate goal. However, the experiments only consider the mean square error in estimating difference of Q.

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Paper is difficult to read with overly complex notation and theorem statements; lacks simplified main result
extracted_weaknesses.quote: Overall, the paper is quite hard to read, even if you have a background in both RL and orthogonal ML. I think the notation could be improved significantly, and the theorem statements are very difficult to parse/understand.

candidate_papers.title: Generative Value Learning (GVL) for Visual RL

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Real-world results show only small improvements over baseline diffusion policy; broader practical value unclear
extracted_weaknesses.quote: The real-world results are not too impressive. Applying GVL to compute values only leads to a small improvement over the based diffusion policy baseline.

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Method requires access to complete video, preventing online policy learning application
extracted_weaknesses.quote: As I understand, calculating the value for each frame requires access to a complete video, which could limit its use in online policy learning without an offline dataset or expert demonstrations.

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Circular reasoning in evaluation: uses OXE dataset to validate GVL performance, then uses GVL+VOC to identify suboptimal datapoints in OXE
extracted_weaknesses.quote: The use of Value Order Correlation (VOC)—the correlation between GVL and frame order—seemed somewhat circular. It is used on the OXE dataset to judge GVL's performance, a choice that assumes that the contents of OXE are of sufficient quality.

extracted_weaknesses.weakness: Limited analysis of GVL's ability in videos with repetition patterns
extracted_weaknesses.quote: It would be good to see more analysis regarding GVL's ability to accurately estimate values in videos where repetition is present. Currently, the existence of such an ability has to be inferred from downstream effects
